transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I feel like I’m worrying about everything lately. My clients, the market, my family, money… even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. It just feels like my level of worry is bigger than what’s actually going on.
Did this increased worrying start after a particular stressful event or change in your life?
Yes, I think it really picked up after I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo. That was about a year and two months ago, and the worrying has kind of been going on since then.
Do your worries mostly center on the move to the condo and its consequences?

Not mostly, no. The condo is part of it, and I do second-guess whether that was the right decision, but it’s broader than that. I worry about clients, the market, my family, money… it just feels like everything, and more than the situation really calls for.
For at least six months, have you felt worried like this on most days?
Yes, definitely more than six months. It’s been about a year and two months now, since after I sold my house and moved into the condo. Most days, yes.
When you start worrying, do you find it hard to stop or control the worry?
Yes. I’ll tell myself, “Parin, this isn’t urgent,” but then one worry turns into another. Before I know it, I’ve spent 30 minutes going over some small detail I meant to just let go.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?
I’m not sure I’d call it restless exactly. I don’t think I’m pacing around or anything. I guess I can feel keyed up sometimes, but I haven’t really paid close attention to that part.
Do you get tired easily?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed getting tired unusually easily, at least not enough that it stands out to me.
Do you find it hard to concentrate because of the worrying?

Yes, I do notice that. When I’m reviewing purchase agreements or inspection addendums, I’ll sometimes read the same paragraph three or four times. A worry pops into my head and I lose track of what I was supposed to be checking.
Have you been more irritable than usual?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get frustrated like anyone does, but I haven’t noticed being more irritable than usual.
Have you been having muscle tension?

Yes, I think so. By the end of the day my neck and shoulders are pretty tight, like I’ve been holding myself tense without realizing it. And sometimes when I’m driving between listings or sitting at my desk, I catch myself clenching my jaw.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes, most nights I get into bed at a reasonable time, but then my mind just keeps going. I’ll think about condo fees, the next day’s showings, or whether I missed something in a contract. It takes me a long time to settle down, and I usually wake up feeling like I didn’t really rest.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless?
Not really, no. I’ve been worried and stressed, but I wouldn’t say I’ve felt depressed or hopeless over the past couple weeks.
Has this worrying been interfering with your work or your day-to-day life?

Yes, it has, mostly at work. Even things that used to feel pretty routine, like going over a contract or handling a listing negotiation, are taking me a lot longer now. I’ll keep rechecking things, and sometimes I put off returning calls because I don’t feel sure I’ve looked everything over carefully enough.
